summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer was admitted for severe nausea and bilious vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake or medications. She had been recently discharged after pacer adjustment but re-presented one week later with recurrent symptoms. Initial management included IV fluids, antiemetics, and insulin adjustment for hyperglycemia. Hypertension and tachycardia were present, likely due to sympathetic activation from nausea. An abdominal X-ray ruled out obstruction, and blood cultures were negative. An endoscopy revealed esophagitis and a tight pylorus, leading to Botox injection for sphincter relaxation. Post-procedure, her nausea improved, allowing advancement to a soft diet. Potassium was repleted for hypokalemia. She was discharged home in stable condition on her prior medications, with follow-up scheduled with GI and endocrinology.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
